reason: Most days I just buy a plate from the stall for 50 baht, no shopping and no washing up, and when I do cook it's easy things like kra pao that I already know by heart. Paying 99 baht every month, that's two plates of food, to learn dishes I can buy around the corner doesn't make sense for my family.
objection: My kitchen is tiny and I have one pan, 'most dishes' is not all of them, and I only cook when I find the time, so I'd never keep up with a new dish every week. I'd be paying every month for an app I open once or twice, when the cooking clips I watch before bed are free.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing in real numbers that cooking the Sunday plan for my family costs clearly less than buying from the stall all week, enough to save a lot more than 99 baht a month.
